_comment: Differences from the published 1.5.5 that the OWNER has accepted, each with a rationale and a kind:
improvement  additive or strictly better; a 1.5.5 client/operator keeps working unchanged
A matching cell reports as ACCEPTED in its own column — never as a silent pass — so a later change
to the same surface still shows. `cells` are id regexes; `classes` limits the acceptance to those
divergence classes (a status or usage change on an 'improvement' entry is still red).
Zero UNACCEPTED divergences is the ship gate.

An entry with `transform: {candidate: [[regex, replacement], ...]}` is line-precise: the candidate's stderr/body text is rewritten before the diff, so only that token is forgiven; the cell reports ACCEPTED, never PASS.
breaking     a deliberate change named in the 1.6.0 CHANGELOG (`changelog` field required) — the ONLY kind that may accept a `status` or `effects.usage` class
The differ refuses any entry that accepts `status` or `effects.usage` without kind=breaking and a `changelog` field, and any entry with neither `cells` nor `classes` (a total blanket).

EVERY entry, improvement or breaking, owes a `changelog` line that appears verbatim in CHANGELOG.md (BUSBAR-1.6.0.md's owner rule accepts an improvement 'named in the CHANGELOG' too), or an explicit `"changelog": null` with a `changelog_reason`; a breaking entry may never waive. scripts/changelog-register-check.sh is the gate.
EVERY entry also carries (1.6.0 items 52/119, Law 10; gate `changelog-register` rows entry-signed / entry-expires / entry-premise):
`signoff`  {who, when, ruling} — the owner, the date, and the ruling that accepted THIS scope; an agent cannot sign.
`expires`  {baseline, by} — the golden baseline the entry forgives against and the date it lapses (re-sign or retire).

`premise`  a condition the runner (busbar-release src/premise.rs, pin 57da1eb) evaluates against the CANDIDATE recording before the entry may forgive: false or unevaluable WITHHOLDS the entry and the cell scores DIVERGING.

accepted.id: F-015 an inline secret is refused without echoing it
accepted.rationale: BOOT-P32 writes an INLINE LITERAL where a secret reference belongs (`providers.gemini.api_key: 7`). 1.5.5 had no scalar visitor on SecretRef, so that value fell through to serde's DEFAULT invalid-type error, which prints the value it was handed: `invalid type: integer `7`, expected a secret reference map: {…}`. The one path this type exists to keep a secret off — stderr and the boot log — is exactly where the rejected secret went, and an unquoted scalar (`api_key: 483920175534`) is the spelling nobody thinks to check. 1.6.0's SecretRef refuses every inline-scalar spelling through one message that states the RULE and never echoes the value: `a secret value must be a REFERENCE, never an inline literal (the value is not echoed): use { env: <VAR> }, { file: <path> }, or { module: <secret-module>, settings: {…} }` (crates/secret-ref/src/lib.rs, RefVisitor::inline_literal). That is the rule the config inventory already documents for every secret-bearing key, so the new sentence tells the operator what to write instead of what serde could not parse. NOT a plane-work side effect: the wording landed on 2026-08-08, long before this branch's base, and reverting it would restore a message that prints an operator's pasted API key into the log. SCOPE: the refusal itself is unchanged — exit code 1, empty stdout, the same `config.yaml: invalid YAML: providers.gemini.api_key: … at line 42 column 14` frame around the sentence, and the same preceding BUSBAR_PROVIDERS deprecation warning byte-for-byte. The `BUSBAR-3015:` prefix on the [error] line is D-1's and is already rewritten away before this entry is consulted. Narrowed to the ONE recorded cell that drives an inline-literal secret; if a fixture ever adds another, name it here explicitly rather than widening the regex to the boot.refusal family.

accepted.id: F-019 a service-account key file that cannot be read is not echoed
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-22 credential-leak triage (parked by the agent with cell, diff, root cause and recommendation; approved on that report -- the path-shaped-heuristic alternative was offered and rejected)

candidate: could not read service-account key file named by this lane's credential
could not read service-account key file <REF>
could not read service-account key file '[^']*'
could not read service-account key file <REF>

accepted.rationale: BOOT-036 drives `auth: jwt-bearer` with an api_key reference the recorder resolves to a value that is not a readable path, so the lane falls to `jwt_bearer::read_credential`'s `fs::read_to_string` arm (crates/busbar-kernel/src/egress_auth/jwt_bearer.rs). 1.5.5 interpolated that ARGUMENT into the failure: `could not read service-account key file '<the argument>': <io error>`. On that branch the argument is a PATH ONLY BY ASSUMPTION -- the sole thing that tells a pasted service-account JSON from a path to one is a leading `{` -- so an operator who pasted the key BODY, or whose `env:`/`file:` reference resolved to key MATERIAL rather than to a filename, reaches that line holding the RS256 SIGNING KEY, and 1.5.5 printed it. REACHABILITY WAS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED, on both ends: the `--validate` / admin config dry-run path reaches it at crates/busbar-kernel/src/config_validate/mod.rs:2194 (`jwt_bearer::validate_credential` -> `parse_service_account` -> `read_credential`), whose Err is pushed into the `errors` list the CLI prints and the dry-run returns; and the boot/apply path reaches it at crates/busbar-llm/src/engine/build_runtime.rs:155, where `jwt_bearer::build(...)` is followed by `.unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("provider for '{}' (jwt-bearer auth): {e}", li.model))` -- so the key also lands in a PANIC MESSAGE and therefore in a crash log. 1.6.0 reports the io failure and nothing else: `could not read service-account key file named by this lane's credential: <io error>`. The caller already names the lane and the secret's configured source (`provider '<name>' jwt-bearer credential (from env:VAR) is invalid: <this>`), so the misconfiguration is exactly as diagnosable and the key is no longer in the output. THE DIVERGENCE IS NOT ELIMINABLE: this cell pins the 1.5.5 SENTENCE, and keeping the argument in that sentence IS the leak -- there is no wording that is both byte-identical to 1.5.5 and not a key disclosure. A 'render it only when it looks path-shaped' heuristic was offered to the owner and REJECTED, on the grounds that a shape guess about the argument is the same assumption that produced the leak. SCOPE IS ONE CELL ID, ANCHORED, and the refusal around it is untouched: exit code 1, empty stdout, the same preceding BUSBAR_PROVIDERS deprecation warning, the same `config validation failed:` frame and the same `provider 'gemini' jwt-bearer credential (from env:ORACLE_UPSTREAM_KEY) is invalid:` prefix, byte for byte. Only the clause naming the unreadable file moves. WHY A `transform` AND NOT F-015's BARE `classes`, which this entry otherwise copies: a bare `classes: [effects.stderr]` would forgive EVERY stderr difference on this cell, and this cell currently carries a SECOND one that is deliberately NOT accepted here. Its `[error]` line reads `[error] BUSBAR-3015: config validation failed:` against the golden's uncoded `[error] config validation failed:`. That prefix is D-1's, already owner-accepted, and F-015's rationale says of the same prefix that it 'is already rewritten away before this entry is consulted'. It is NOT being rewritten away today: D-1's transform replacement is written `\1 ` (Python `re.sub` backreference syntax), and the Phase-C Rust judge rewrites through `regex::Regex::replace_all`, whose replacer spells a capture `$1` and emits a literal `\1` for anything else -- so the candidate's line becomes the literal `\1 config validation failed:` and still diverges. That is a judge/register syntax mismatch introduced by the Python->Rust cutover, it is D-1's to repair (one character, `\1` -> `$1`, across ~462 cells in D-1's scope -- an owner-sized movement), and it is NOT approved by this entry. The two transform rules below collapse BOTH sides' key-file clause to a single `<REF>` token, so this entry forgives exactly that clause and leaves the `[error]`-prefix difference to report itself. [UPDATE 2026-09-22, after this entry was written: D-1's rewrite HAS been repaired, but NOT the way this rationale proposed. Do NOT edit the register's `\1` to `$1` -- the register is shared with the Python reference differ, where `$1` is not a backreference and the edit would break it there. The repair translates the Python template at the LOAD boundary instead (`\1`..`\99`, `\g<name>`, `\\`, `$`->`$$`), and refuses an untranslatable entry rather than silently substituting empty, which is what Rust's regex would have done. Measured effect: effects.stderr divergences fell 190 -> 3 on a 630-cell candidate, and 203 of 206 on the full 916-cell baseline carried the artifact, with ZERO newly-red cells. The judge pin moved to that fix in the same pass.] ONCE D-1'S REWRITE IS REPAIRED this entry may be simplified to F-015's exact shape -- drop `transform`, keep `classes` -- and the cell will report ACCEPTED rather than diverging.

accepted.id: 581 busbar is invisible to upstreams except what it governs
accepted.changelog: busbar is invisible to upstreams. On a same-dialect route every client header and body field passes through unchanged, except the fields busbar governs: credential headers (each dialect declares its own, e.g. Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, x-goog-api-key), replaced by busbar's upstream credential; tenant selectors (e.g. OpenAI-Organization, OpenAI-Project), set from busbar's config and never from the caller; the model, which is mapped; hook rewrites; and the HTTP hop-by-hop headers plus Host and Content-Length, re-derived for the upstream connection. On a translated route busbar translates what maps and drops the rest. There are no feature allowlists; beta and version headers are ordinary fields. 1.5.5 forwarded no client header.
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-10-02 HARD RULE "BUSBAR IS INVISIBLE TO UPSTREAMS" (escalate.q 03:40Z, refined 04:00Z)
accepted.rationale: Same-dialect routes forward every client header and body field; 1.5.5 forwarded no client header. The two cells send an anthropic-beta / openai-beta header on a same-dialect route: 1.5.5's upstream request carries neither, the candidate's carries `anthropic-beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31` / `openai-beta: assistants=v2` and nothing else differs. The translated route (egress.headers|forwarded|anthropic-beta-cross) is identical to 1.5.5 and is NOT in scope: it carries no beta header on either build. The cells for the invisible-upstream rule's other fields (INVISIBLE-UPSTREAM card) join `cells` when recorded. Premise: the same-dialect upstream really carries the header, the translated one does not. KIND NOTE: the signed draft said `additive`, but the additive judge requires the candidate's arrays to be a position-wise superset of 1.5.5's, and the forwarded header lands mid-list (before host and content-length), so C13/C14 scored FAIL `additive: not a superset at /upstream/0/headers/5/0`; `improvement` (additive or strictly better, per this file's own legend) is the kind the register can express.
